components.name: header
components.description: The literal sk, then a dot.

components.name: payload
components.description: A base64url-encoded JSON object holding a reference to the token's metadata. Its length is not documented.

components.name: signature
components.description: Signed by Mapbox. Its encoding and length are not documented.

claims.statement: A secret access token is a string of three dot-delimited parts (header, payload, signature) whose header is the literal sk.

sources.supports: Each token is a string delimited by dots into three parts: header, payload, and signature; the header is a literal value of either pk, sk or tk.
All secret access tokens start with sk.

claims.statement: The payload of a secret access token is a base64url-encoded JSON object that holds a reference to the metadata recording the token's rights, not the metadata itself.

sources.supports: The payload is a base64-URL-encoded JSON object containing the identity and authorities of the token; pk and sk tokens contain a reference to metadata that holds the rights granted for the token.

claims.statement: The signature part of a secret access token is signed by Mapbox so that tampering can be detected.

sources.supports: The signature is signed by Mapbox and used to verify the token has not been tampered with.

openQuestions.question: What encoding and length does the signature part have? The documentation names neither.
Does the payload part have a fixed or bounded length? The documentation states none.
Has the token format changed over time, and are older secret tokens in circulation with a different shape? The documentation read carries no change history.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Only what the provider's documentation states is recorded as a claim; no alphabet or length is declared because no source gives one for the whole token.
